title: Asexual and Sexual Reproduction
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Asexual and Sexual Reproduction Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Cells are derived from cells: the cell cycle and mitosis, asexual reproduction, meiosis and sexual reproduction, and the advantages of each. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 9, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 science worksheets (BC): the cell cycle, mitosis, asexual reproduction, meiosis, sexual reproduction in plants and animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mitosis copies cells; meiosis makes sex cells.
key_sub: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents.
body_html:
How to think about it

In mitosis one cell divides into two identical cells with the same number of chromosomes. It is used for growth and repair, and for asexual reproduction, where one parent makes offspring that are genetically identical (binary fission, budding, runners, cuttings).

Meiosis makes sex cells (gametes) with half the number of chromosomes: 23 in humans. In sexual reproduction two gametes join at fertilization, so the offspring get a mix of genes from two parents. This variation helps a population survive change.

Example

A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many does a sperm cell have?

Meiosis halves the number.

Answer: 23

Example

A strawberry plant grows new plants from runners. What kind of reproduction is this?

Only one parent

Answer: asexual

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mitosis and meiosis.
  • Thinking asexual offspring are different from the parent.
  • Thinking sexual reproduction is faster.

faq.q: What is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
faq.a: It is fast and needs only one parent.
If the environment changes, some individuals may have traits that help them survive.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cell looks pinched in the middle as it splits in two.
items.e: Cytokinesis: The cell looks pinched in the middle as it splits in two.

items.q: What forms the spindle in animal cells?
items.e: Plant cells form a spindle without centrioles.

items.q: What is the significance of mitosis?
c: creating genetic variation by crossing over
growth, repair and keeping the chromosome number the same
items.e: It replaces worn-out cells.

items.q: Which stage is this? Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends of the cell.
items.e: Anaphase: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends of the cell.

items.q: Which stage is this? DNA is replicated during the S stage.
items.e: Interphase: DNA is replicated during the S stage.

items.q: Which stage is this? Spindle fibres attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.
items.e: Metaphase: Spindle fibres attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.

items.q: What is the significance of meiosis?
c: it halves the chromosome number for gametes and creates variation
items.e: Fertilization restores the diploid number.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)?
items.e: Metaphase: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate).

items.q: Which stage comes right after telophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cytoplasm splits and two daughter cells form.
items.e: Cytokinesis: The cytoplasm splits and two daughter cells form.

items.q: Which stage comes right before prophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage comes right after prophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What happens in S phase?
c: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
items.e: S phase: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles?
items.e: S phase: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles.

items.q: How long does a typical human cell cycle take in culture?
items.e: Yeast takes only about 90 minutes.

items.q: At which stage are chromosomes best studied?
items.e: They are most condensed then.

items.q: Which stage is this? Two new nuclei form around the chromosomes at each end.
items.e: Telophase: Two new nuclei form around the chromosomes at each end.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells?
items.e: Cytokinesis: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes?
items.e: Telophase: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes.

items.q: Which stage comes right after interphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: A fruit fly cell has 8 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 8 × 2 = 16.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 12 hours. In a sample, 20 of 300 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 20/300 × 720 min = 48.0 min.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 60 of 300 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 20.0%.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 12 hours. In a sample, 36 of 240 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 36/240 × 720 min = 108 min.

items.q: A human cell has 46 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 46 × 2 = 92.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing?
items.e: G₂ phase: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing.

items.q: Which enzyme helps crossing over?
items.e: Crossing over is between non-sister chromatids.

items.q: A mouse body cell has 40 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell after mitosis?
items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: A corn cell has 20 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 20 × 2 = 40.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 36 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 9.00%.

items.q: A garden onion cell with 16 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 16 = 32.

items.q: A potato body cell has 48 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell after mitosis?
items.e: Mitosis makes identical cells with the same number.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 18 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 4.50%.

items.q: What happens in telophase?
c: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
items.e: Telophase: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 20 of 500 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 4.00%.

items.q: Which division is called equational division?
items.e: The chromosome number stays the same.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 20 hours. In a sample, 20 of 250 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 20/250 × 1200 min = 96.0 min.

items.q: For mitosis, what is the number of daughter cells made?
c: identical to each other and the parent
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: Why do offspring from sexual reproduction show variation?
c: They get half their chromosomes from each parent, in new combinations.
They are copies of one parent.
items.e: Mixing creates variation.

items.q: Owen reads: “A frog's egg is fertilized by sperm.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
It will be identical to one parent's.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For a sperm cell, what is the size?
c: large, one of the largest human cells
an acrosome with enzymes to digest the egg's outer layer
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: Hana reads: “A potato sprouts new plants from its eyes.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
It will be identical to the parent's.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

c: identical to each other and the parent
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: For meiosis, what is its role?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

a jelly coat that changes after one sperm enters
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

an acrosome with enzymes to digest the egg's outer layer

items.q: Ava reads: “Salmon release eggs and sperm in a stream.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: For meiosis, what is the chromosome number of the daughter cells?
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: For meiosis, what is where it happens in humans?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
in body cells for growth and repair
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.

large, one of the largest human cells
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

items.q: What is an allele?
c: a different version of the same gene
items.e: For example, B or b.

items.q: What is one advantage of sexual reproduction?
c: Variation helps some offspring survive if the environment changes.
items.e: Variation is useful.

items.q: How many sets of chromosomes does a human get from each parent?
c: one set (23 chromosomes) from each parent

items.q: For meiosis, what is the number of daughter cells made?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: A potato cell (2n = 48) finishes meiosis I. How many chromosomes are in each of the two new cells?
items.e: Homologs separate in meiosis I, so each cell has 24 (each still with two chromatids).

items.q: A chimpanzee body cell has 48 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
A fruit fly body cell has 8 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 4.

items.q: What happens in leptotene of meiosis?
c: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
chromosomes become visible as thin threads
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
items.e: Leptotene: chromosomes become visible as thin threads.

items.q: How does cytokinesis happen in plant cells?
c: a cell plate forms in the middle and grows outward
a furrow forms from the outside
items.e: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow.

items.q: How many chromatids are present in a bivalent?
items.e: A bivalent is a pair of homologous chromosomes, each with two chromatids.

items.q: A potato egg and sperm each have 24 chromosomes. How many does the fertilized egg have?
A dog cell (2n = 78) finishes meiosis I. How many chromosomes are in each of the two new cells?
items.e: Homologs separate in meiosis I, so each cell has 39 (each still with two chromatids).

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous pairs line up in the middle of the cell.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: Mitosis: are the new cells identical?
items.e: Meiosis: no, genetically different. Mitosis: yes, identical.

items.q: What happens in diplotene of meiosis?
c: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
chromosomes become visible as thin threads
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
items.e: Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: chromosomes become visible as thin threads?
items.e: Leptotene: chromosomes become visible as thin threads.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes pair up and swap pieces (crossing over).
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Single chromosomes line up in the middle of two cells.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Sister chromatids separate to opposite poles.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A fruit fly body cell has 8 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
items.e: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 pairs.

items.q: A rice cell (2n = 24) finishes meiosis I. How many chromosomes are in each of the two new cells?
items.e: Homologs separate in meiosis I, so each cell has 12 (each still with two chromatids).

items.q: Mitosis: chromosome number in new cells?
items.e: Meiosis: half (haploid). Mitosis: same (diploid).

items.q: Meiosis: main purpose?
items.e: Meiosis: making gametes for sexual reproduction. Mitosis: growth and repair.

items.q: What happens in anaphase II of meiosis?
c: chiasmata terminalize and the nuclear envelope breaks down
the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
chromosomes become visible as thin threads
sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
items.e: Anaphase II: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: What is a bone marrow transplant for leukaemia?
c: a current use of adult stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: mRNA: UUUUGGAAU. Codons: AAU = Asn, UGG = Trp, UUU = Phe, GCU = Ala. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UUU UGG AAU.

items.q: What is an oncogene?
c: a gene that stops cell division
a mutated proto-oncogene that is permanently switched on
items.e: It causes cells to divide too fast.

items.q: What is the difference between benign and malignant tumours?
c: benign tumours spread around the body
malignant tumours invade tissues and spread (metastasis)
items.e: Benign tumours are usually enclosed.

items.q: Which statement about adult stem cells from bone marrow is true?
c: They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.

items.q: mRNA: UUUGGUGCU. Codons: GCU = Ala, GGU = Gly, UUU = Phe, ACU = Thr, UAU = Tyr. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UUU GGU GCU.

items.q: Which statement about meristem tissue in plants is true?
c: They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: How can a substitution mutation stop a protein working?
c: it always makes the protein longer
it may change an amino acid in the active site so the shape changes
items.e: Or it may create a stop codon.

items.q: An embryo's cells become heart, nerve and skin cells. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialized.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become almost any type of cell?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: There are ethical objections because embryos are destroyed.

items.q: What is a stem cell?
c: an undifferentiated cell that can divide and become specialized
items.e: Totipotent, pluripotent, multipotent and unipotent cells.

items.q: What does siRNA do?
c: guides an enzyme to cut a complementary mRNA
items.e: The mRNA cannot then be translated.

items.q: mRNA: UCUUUUAAU. Codons: AAU = Asn, UCU = Ser, UUU = Phe, AGC = Ser, UUC = Phe. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UCU UUU AAU.

items.q: mRNA: GCUAUUUAU. Codons: AUU = Ile, GCU = Ala, UAU = Tyr, UUU = Phe. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: GCU AUU UAU.

a use of plant stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: What is growing crops with special features, such as disease resistance?

a current use of adult stem cells
a possible future use of stem cells

items.q: What is cloning rare plants quickly and cheaply from meristems?

a current use of adult stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: What is a transcription factor?
c: an enzyme that joins amino acids
a protein that binds to DNA and switches transcription of a gene on or off
items.e: It binds near the gene's promoter.
